clues: Spring paints a moving trail of pink across these islands as cherry blossoms open from south to north.
Look off the eastern coast of Asia: a long island chain where bullet trains zip past volcanic mountains.
Mount Fuji watches over this island nation. Think sushi, shinkansen and a red circle on a white flag.
fact: Cherry blossom season travels north through Japan, so different regions bloom at different times.

clues: A giant red rock rises from the desert here, while an astonishing coral world waits off the northeast coast.
Head south of Indonesia to a huge landmass between the Indian and Pacific oceans. Kangaroos call it home.
The Great Barrier Reef and Sydney's sail-shaped Opera House belong to this country. X marks the land Down Under.
fact: Sydney Opera House's famous roofs are groups of interlocking vaulted shells, designed by Jørn Utzon.

clues: Pack your binoculars: an alpine parrot called the kea lives among this country's mountains and glacial valleys.
Search the southwest Pacific, southeast of Australia, for two large islands with fjords and snowy peaks.
Aotearoa is another name for this country. Its famous kiwi is a flightless bird, not just a fruit.
fact: The kiwi has hair-like feathers, strong legs and no tail, and is a cherished national symbol.

clues: Your treasure trail climbs from Pacific shores into the Andes, where ancient stone settlements cling to the heights.
This South American country was the heart of the Inca Empire. It shares Lake Titicaca with Bolivia.
Follow the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu. Which country holds this mountaintop treasure?
fact: The Machu Picchu sanctuary protects cloud forests as well as the Inca archaeological site.

clues: A thunderous waterfall frontier is one treasure here; another is a coastal city tucked between mountains and sea.
Find the largest country in South America. Portuguese is spoken here, and much of the Amazon lies within it.
Christ the Redeemer spreads its arms above Rio de Janeiro in this country, home to Copacabana beach.
fact: Rio's World Heritage landscape includes mountains, botanical gardens and the sweeping shore of Copacabana.

clues: Some forests here are made of towering cacti, and ancient cities hold stone temples and underground water wells.
Look in North America, directly south of the United States, with Pacific and Caribbean shores.
The Maya city of Chichén Itzá and its stepped pyramid, El Castillo, are waiting in this country's Yucatán Peninsula.
fact: Chichén Itzá grew near natural wells called cenotes, which gave its residents access to underground water.

clues: An unexpected treasure hides in these Rocky Mountains: fossils of sea creatures that lived over 500 million years ago.
Find the vast North American country above the United States, stretching from the Atlantic to the Pacific.
Its flag has a red maple leaf. Banff's mountain lakes and Québec's old streets are both in this country.
fact: The Burgess Shale preserves remarkable fossils of ancient marine animals, high in the Rocky Mountains.

clues: A treasure of bubbling springs and erupting geysers was protected here as a national park back in 1872.
Look between Canada and Mexico for a country whose mainland reaches both the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
The Grand Canyon, Yellowstone and the Statue of Liberty all belong to this country of 50 states.
fact: Yellowstone National Park was established in 1872 and lies mostly in the state of Wyoming.

clues: A volcano buried Roman towns here in AD 79, leaving an extraordinary time capsule for future treasure hunters.
One of its cities spreads across a lagoon on small islands, with canals threading between palaces.
Find the boot kicking into the Mediterranean. Venice, Pompeii and the Leaning Tower of Pisa are all here.
fact: Venice grew across 118 small islands in a lagoon, linked by its network of waterways.

clues: A medieval abbey crowns a rocky islet here, surrounded by sandbanks that powerful tides can cover.
This western European country has Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts; the Louvre guards some of its art treasures.
The Eiffel Tower is your final beacon. Find its country, across the Channel from the United Kingdom.
fact: Mont-Saint-Michel's abbey was built over centuries on a rocky islet between Normandy and Brittany.

clues: Ancient temples here told stories of gods and goddesses, and carved stone columns still stand above a busy city.
Search southeastern Europe, where a jagged peninsula reaches into the Mediterranean beside the Aegean Sea.
The Parthenon, Mount Olympus and the islands of Crete and Santorini point to this country.
fact: The Parthenon is part of the Acropolis complex, whose major monuments were built in the fifth century BC.

clues: Sail between cliffs that rise like giant castle walls: glaciers carved deep sea inlets into this coastline.
Look along the western side of Scandinavia, beside Sweden, with a long coastline reaching far into the Arctic.
This is the country of Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord. Its flag is red with a blue cross outlined in white.
fact: The West Norwegian Fjords have steep rock walls, waterfalls and landscapes shaped by glaciers.

clues: Long before modern parliament buildings, people gathered outdoors here to make laws at an assembly founded in 930.
Find a volcanic island in the North Atlantic, east of Greenland, where glaciers share the landscape with hot springs.
The land of fire and ice has geysers, black-sand beaches and the Blue Lagoon. Look just below the Arctic Circle.
fact: The Althing assembly began meeting at Þingvellir in 930 and met there for centuries.

clues: Ancient rulers built enormous stone tombs here, turning their desert resting places into landmarks for the ages.
Trace the Nile through northeastern Africa to the Mediterranean. This country also touches the Red Sea.
The pyramids of Giza and the Great Sphinx guard your final clue. Which country is their home?
fact: The pyramid fields from Giza to Dahshur form part of a World Heritage site linked to ancient Memphis.

clues: One mountain town here is famous for blue-painted lanes, while old walled cities hide gardens and bustling squares.
Look in northwest Africa, across the Strait of Gibraltar from Spain, with both Atlantic and Mediterranean shores.
Marrakesh, Casablanca and the blue town of Chefchaouen are all in this country beside the Atlas Mountains.
fact: Marrakesh's medina contains monumental gateways, gardens and the open-air square of Jamaâ El Fna.

clues: Here is a safari surprise: a national park has wild animals roaming with a modern city's skyline behind them.
Look in East Africa, on the equator and the Indian Ocean, directly north of Tanzania.
The Maasai Mara's big cats and wildebeest are a famous treasure here. Find Tanzania's neighbor to the northeast.
fact: Nairobi National Park protects wildlife habitat close enough to the city for skyscrapers to frame the view.

clues: Vast herds of wildebeest and zebras follow the rains across these grasslands, with hungry predators on their trail.
Head to East Africa, south of Kenya. This country has Indian Ocean shores and the islands of Zanzibar.
Mount Kilimanjaro and Serengeti National Park are both here. Find the country holding Africa's highest summit.
fact: The Serengeti's great migration includes wildebeest, zebras and gazelles moving in search of water and grazing.

clues: Not every forest has leaves: this country's tsingy landscapes contain a maze of sharp limestone pinnacles.
Look for a large island in the Indian Ocean, off southeastern Africa and across the water from Mozambique.
Lemurs and towering baobab trees are the stars of this island country, just east of mainland Africa.
fact: The Andrefana Dry Forests protect limestone landscapes, baobabs and habitats for rare lemurs.

clues: Even fetching water could mean descending into a work of art: a carved stepwell here was designed like an inverted temple.
Search South Asia for a broad peninsula, with the Himalayas to its north and Sri Lanka just off its southern tip.
The white marble Taj Mahal in Agra is the final treasure on your trail. Which country is it in?
fact: Rani-ki-Vav, the Queen's Stepwell, has seven levels of stairs decorated with intricate sculptural panels.

clues: Snow leopards and red pandas share this country's mountain wilderness with glaciers and deep Himalayan valleys.
This landlocked South Asian country sits between India and China; Sherpa communities live in its high mountains.
Everest climbers take the southern approach through this country. Find the narrow Himalayan neighbor north of India.
fact: Sagarmatha National Park protects Himalayan landscapes and wildlife on the southern side of Mount Everest.

clues: A defensive treasure snakes across hills here: rulers linked older fortifications, then later dynasties kept building.
Find a vast East Asian country south of Mongolia, with a Pacific coastline and giant pandas among its native wildlife.
The Great Wall is your unmistakable landmark. Which country built this sprawling system of ancient defenses?
fact: The Great Wall was built and rebuilt over many centuries, with major construction continuing under the Ming dynasty.

clues: An ancient empire left a treasure trail of reservoirs, canals and stone temples hidden among forests here.
Look in mainland Southeast Asia, between Thailand and Vietnam, for the historic heartland of the Khmer Empire.
The towers of Angkor Wat are your final beacon. Find the country that holds this famous temple complex.
fact: The Angkor area includes not only temples but reservoirs, dykes, canals and roads from the Khmer Empire.

clues: A huge ancient Buddhist temple rises here in tiers of stone, with dozens of bell-shaped stupas circling its upper levels.
Follow the islands of Sumatra and Java across the equator, between mainland Southeast Asia and Australia.
Bali, Java and the Komodo dragons' islands all belong to this sprawling island country.
fact: Borobudur in central Java has 72 openwork stupas around its circular platforms, each containing a Buddha statue.

clues: Your boat could weave between limestone towers rising from the sea in one of this country's spectacular bays.
Find a long, narrow country on mainland Southeast Asia's eastern coast, beside Laos and Cambodia and south of China.
Ha Long Bay lies in its north and the Mekong Delta in its south. Look for the S-shaped country on the coast.
fact: Ha Long Bay and the Cat Ba Archipelago contain a dramatic seascape of limestone islands and islets.
